What it does

This law requires healthcare providers and healthcare facilities to tell patients when artificial intelligence is used to document in person or telehealth visits. It also requires those providers and facilities to review the AI generated documentation for accuracy after the visit.

Who it applies to

  • Healthcare providers as defined in 23-106-2(3)
  • Healthcare facilities as defined in 23-106-2(2)

Effective date

upon passage (Sec. 2)

Key definitions

  • Artificial Intelligence or AI: any technology that can simulate human intelligence including, but not limited to, natural language processing, training language models, reinforcement learning from human feedback and machine learning systems (23-106-2(1))
  • Healthcare facility: has the same meaning as in § 23-17-2 (23-106-2(2))
  • Healthcare provider: physicians, physician assistants, dentists, registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, nursing assistants, or any other healthcare professional licensed by the director of the department of health (23-106-2(3))

Obligations

  • Notify patients of the use of AI for the sole purpose of documenting in person or telehealth visits (23-106-3)
  • Review the AI generated documentation for accuracy after the visit (23-106-3)

Prohibitions

  • No explicit prohibitions are stated in the text.

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • A healthcare provider or healthcare facility that uses AI to document in person or telehealth visits must give notice to patients of that use for that sole purpose (23-106-3)
  • The provider or facility must review the AI generated documentation for accuracy after the visit (23-106-3)
  • The law does not specify any penalty or enforcement mechanism for noncompliance (not stated in the text)

Notable exemptions

  • No exemptions are stated in the text.

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organization uses AI to document in person or telehealth visits (23-106-3)
  • Notify patients of the use of AI for that sole purpose (23-106-3)
  • Review the AI generated documentation for accuracy after the visit (23-106-3)

 STATE OF RHODE ISLAND

 IN GENERAL ASSEMBLY

 JANUARY SESSION, A.D. 2026
 ____________


 AN ACT

 RELATING TO HEALTH AND SAFETY -- USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BY
 HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS NOTIFICATION ACT



 Introduced By: Representatives Tanzi, McGaw, Felix, Hull, J. Lombardi, Stewart,
 Giraldo, Edwards, Bennett, and Diaz
 Date Introduced: February 06, 2026

 Referred To: House Health & Human Services




 It is enacted by the General Assembly as follows:

 1 SECTION 1. Title 23 of the General Laws entitled "HEALTH AND SAFETY" is hereby

 2 amended by adding thereto the following chapter:

 3 CHAPTER 106

 4 USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE BY HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS NOTIFICATION

 5 ACT

 6 23-106-1. Short title and purpose.

 7 (a) This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "Use of Artificial Intelligence by

 8 Healthcare Providers Notification Act".

 9 (b) The purpose of this chapter is to ensure patients are properly notified of the use of

10 artificial intelligence by healthcare providers.

11 23-106-2. Definitions.

12 As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the following meanings:

13 (1) "Artificial Intelligence" or "AI" means any technology that can simulate human

14 intelligence including, but not limited to, natural language processing, training language models,

15 reinforcement learning from human feedback and machine learning systems.

16 (2) "Healthcare facility" shall have the same meaning as § 23-17-2.

17 (3) "Healthcare provider" means physicians, physician assistants, dentists, registered

18 nurses, licensed practical nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, nursing assistants, or any
 1 other healthcare professional licensed by the director of the department of health.

2 23-106-3. Notifications required.

3 Any and all healthcare providers and healthcare facilities that employ artificial intelligence

4 ("AI") to document in-person or telehealth visits shall notify patients of the use of AI for that sole

5 purpose and review the AI-generated documentation for accuracy after the visit.

6 SECTION 2. This act shall take effect upon passage.
